subject: Re: Unplanned p99 latency spikes and OOMs impacting NimbusAI production
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@nimbus.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: ops@nimbus.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T08:12:00-04:00
Subject: p99 spikes + 503s this morning — production impact

Markus / Redwood team,

We started seeing a sustained p95/p99 tail increase and intermittent 503s from your Hosted API in our EU region starting ~07:40 UTC this morning. Our user-facing inference rate dropped ~20% and several batches failed with OOMs in our ops logs. This is causing request retries and customer complaints.

I've attached a quick metrics snapshot and a slice of the service logs showing repeated "CUDA out of memory" + fragmentation messages from your runtime. Can someone confirm whether this is a model-side regression or an infra problem on Redwood's side?

We need an ETA for mitigation and whether we should failover to our fallback model inside the next hour. This is currently P1 for us.

Thanks — Sam

--
Samantha Cho
Head of Platform
NimbusAI
From: laura_bennett@redwood.com
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@nimbus.ai>
Cc: markus_klein@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com, monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-02T08:28:00-04:00
Subject: Re: p99 spikes + 503s this morning — production impact

Sam — thanks for the quick heads up and the attachments. I'm escalating immediately; apologies for the disruption.

What we are doing now:
- Eng running triage on the runtime cluster (Rishi)
- CS coordinating on-the-clock updates for Nimbus (that's me)
- Ops contact for potential credits and rollback options (Markus / Monica)

Can you confirm whether the traffic in the attached snapshot is all inference calls (no embeddings) and whether the failing requests are consistently for the same model version? That will help narrow the surface.

I'll push an update in 20–30 minutes.

Laura Bennett
Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, markus_klein@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-02T09:01:00-04:00
Subject: Re: p99 spikes + 503s this morning — production impact

Laura / Markus — quick technical summary from initial triage:

Findings:
- Multiple worker pods on the eu-west-1 Hosted pool reported repeated CUDA OOMs starting 07:38–07:42 UTC. The runtime logged "memory fragmentation" warnings immediately before OOMs.
- The affected pods are serving a quantized 13B variant used by Nimbus (model tag: nimbus-13b-q4_1).
- OOMs correlate with long requests that build large KV caches (conversation histories ~5–8k tokens).
- Autoscaler did not immediately replace the flapping pods due to a cooldown config; several pods accumulated fragmentation and OOMs before being cycled.

Immediate mitigations executed (09:00 UTC):
- Forced rolling restart of the affected worker set to reclaim fragmented GPU memory.
- Scoped a temporary rate limit on request max_tokens for Nimbus routes to reduce single-request memory pressure.
- Enabled fallback routing to a smaller 6B model variant for new sessions (non-destructive, opt-in).

Next steps:
- Engineering will collect full device-level heap dumps and allocator traces (OOM excerpts attached).
- Ops to evaluate reducing pod cooldown and adjust autoscaler behavior to more aggressively replace flapping workers.
- Recommend a scheduled quantization profile review: q4_1 appears sensitive to fragmentation with long KV sequences. Consider q4_0 or a different caching strategy.

ETA: stabilizing p99 expected within 60–90 minutes if no further fragmentation events occur; full root cause postmortem in 72 hours.

--
Rishi Malhotra
Senior SRE, Inference Runtime
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@nimbus.ai>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, rishi_malhotra@redwood.com
Cc: monica_patel@redwood.com
Date: 2026-08-02T11:04:00-04:00
Subject: Re: p99 spikes + 503s this morning — production impact

Sam — first, I'm very sorry for the disruption. We take incidents like this seriously. Thank you and your team for the detailed logs; they helped us find the memory-fragmentation pattern quickly.

Actions and offers:
- We executed the rolling restarts and temporary throttles Rishi mentioned; those brought p99 back toward baseline by ~09:45 UTC in eu-west-1.
- We're opening an incident ticket (INF-4821) and will share a full RCA and remediation plan within 72 hours.
- As a gesture for the production impact, we'd like to offer a one-time account credit equivalent to 10% of last month's Hosted API spend for Nimbus. Monica, please coordinate finance and credit issuance.

I will also schedule a short exec sync this week to walk through mitigation and the long-term plan (kernel/allocator changes, autoscaler tuning, model quantization guidance). Laura — please keep Sam updated series of in-flight notes.

Sincerely,
Markus Klein
VP, Customer Success & Commercial Operations
Redwood Inference
From: Samantha Cho <samantha.cho@nimbus.ai>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: ops@nimbus.ai
Date: 2026-08-02T16:45:00-04:00
Subject: Re: p99 spikes + 503s this morning — production impact

Markus / Laura — thank you for the fast response and the credit offer. The rolling restart plus throttles did help; our engineering team reported latency back to expected levels after 09:50 UTC. We'll accept the credit and look forward to the RCA (INF-4821).

Please include in your postmortem: the exact autoscaler settings that delayed pod replacement, the allocator traces showing fragmentation, and recommendations for preventing similar memory churn (quantization/profile guidance + best practices for long-KV sessions).

I'll share a short summary to our leadership and will wait for your RCA link.

Best,
Sam
